answer:
Static batching waits for a group of requests and runs them together. When one response ends early, its slot can remain idle while longer responses continue. Continuous batching makes a new scheduling decision each decoding iteration: remove finished requests and admit waiting work. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180)

For lengths 10 and 100, a static two-slot batch has 90 unused sequence-steps after the short response finishes. Reusing that slot improves occupancy. Chunked prefill can interleave long prompt work with decode iterations to reduce stalls.

Throughput alone is insufficient: optimize time-to-first-token, inter-token latency, queue delay, and tail response time. Large batches consume more KV memory and can delay interactive requests. Fairness, maximum waiting time, token budgets, and cache-aware admission keep long or high-volume tenants from monopolizing the server. [2](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)
